Activation patching offers intervention-specific evidence, not automatic identification of a meaningful mechanism. [Zhang and Nanda (ICLR 2024)](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=Hf17y6u9BC) show localization depends strongly on corruption methods and output metrics; [Heimersheim and Nanda (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255) distinguish restoration from disruption and discuss interpretive pitfalls. A [2026 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27510) further finds that interactions among mediators can hide or inflate component importance. Search found no direct validation of these methods for NextItNet; transferring conclusions from language models remains a hypothesis.

Proposed NextItNet protocol: use one frozen checkpoint per category, evaluation mode, and identical candidates throughout. First verify same-history identity patches reproduce unpatched scores within numerical tolerance. Patch clearly specified residual-block outputs at aligned nonpadding positions; read predictions from the final nonpadding position. Choose natural-history donors matched on observable history length, recent-item overlap, timing and item-frequency profile, while varying the hypothesized signal. Test both donor-to-recipient restoration and reverse disruption, alongside matched unrelated-donor controls. Measure raw target-versus-competitor score changes and ranking changes; retain macro validation HR@10 for model selection. These are proposed adaptations, not established NextItNet findings.

Report eligible-recipient coverage, successful matches, unique donors, donor reuse and matching distances per category. Compare patched and natural downstream activation norms, standardized distances and nearest-neighbor distances: natural donor activations can still create unnatural hybrid states. Strong effects concentrated in activation outliers suggest intervention artifacts. Consistent bidirectional effects across donors, with identity checks passing and limited distribution shift, strengthen—but do not prove—a mechanism claim; joint-site tests can expose interactions missed by isolated patches.
